sections.problem: In this fictional scenario, a community workshop has limited seats. Manual signup messages can produce duplicate bookings and leave canceled seats unused.
sections.users: Participants who sign up for a workshop and an organizer who manages its seat limit.
sections.outcomes: Participants can see seat availability, sign up once and join a waitlist when the workshop is full. Canceled seats can be offered fairly. These are intended outcomes, not measured results.
sections.useCases:
UC-01: A participant checks availability and signs up.
UC-02: A participant joins the waitlist.
UC-03: A participant cancels and a waitlisted participant receives an offer.
sections.scope: One fictional workshop session with a fixed seat limit. Include signup, duplicate prevention, waitlist entry, cancellation and offers for released seats.
sections.nonGoals: Payments, recurring sessions, real notifications, attendee exports and integration with external event services.
sections.inputsOutputs: Inputs: the chosen session and a participant’s signup, waitlist or cancellation action. Outputs: a confirmed seat, waitlist position, cancellation result or seat offer.

requirements.outcome: Participants know whether a seat is available.
requirements.behavior: Show the number of seats still available.
requirements.acceptance: The displayed count equals the seat limit minus confirmed signups. When no seats remain, the session is shown as full.

requirements.outcome: The workshop stays within its seat limit.
requirements.behavior: Confirm a participant’s signup only when a seat is available, and prevent duplicate signups.
requirements.acceptance: The same participant receives at most one confirmed seat. Repeating a signup does not consume another seat. When two requests compete for the last seat, at most one is confirmed.

requirements.outcome: Participants can wait for a released seat.
requirements.behavior: Let a participant join the waitlist when the session is full.
requirements.acceptance: A participant can join once and see their position. A repeated request does not create another waitlist entry.

requirements.outcome: A canceled booking can be offered to someone else.
requirements.behavior: Release a seat when its confirmed participant cancels.
requirements.acceptance: Cancellation removes that participant’s confirmed signup and releases exactly one seat. Repeating the cancellation does not release another seat.

requirements.outcome: Waitlisted participants receive a fair chance to join.
requirements.behavior: Offer a released seat to the first participant on the waitlist.
requirements.acceptance: Offers follow waitlist order and only one participant holds an active offer for a seat. The offer expiry and response method still need a decision before this requirement can be tested.

requirements.behavior: Allow participants to cancel only their own signup.
requirements.acceptance: A participant can cancel their own signup. An attempt to cancel another participant’s signup is rejected without changing either record.

sections.quality: Seat counts and signup decisions must stay consistent when requests arrive together. Core actions must work with a keyboard. Error messages must preserve the participant’s current state.
sections.metrics: Proposed measures: duplicate confirmed signups, signups above the seat limit and released seats filled from the waitlist. Baselines and targets are not documented.
sections.risks: An offer with no agreed expiry could block a released seat indefinitely. Concurrent requests could overbook a session if the seat check and confirmation are separate.
sections.decisions: Decide the offer expiry and response method. Confirm how an organizer resolves a disputed waitlist position.
sections.evidence: This PRD is entirely fictional. Its review verdicts, proof and attachments are simulated examples. No real product, user research or test result is represented.
